description: This file contains Celery task definitions and helper functions for executing SQL queries asynchronously within the Superset project. It manages query execution, error handling, result serialization, and storage in the results backend.

classes.name: Query
classes.description: Model representing a SQL query in Superset.

classes.name: SupersetResultSet
classes.description: Class representing the result set of a SQL query.

methods.name: _get_query
methods.description: Retrieve a Query object by its ID from the database.

methods.name: _handle_query_error
methods.description: Handle exceptions during query execution, update query status, and prepare error payload.

methods.name: _serialize_payload
methods.description: Serialize the payload for storage, using msgpack or JSON based on configuration.

methods.name: _prepare_statement_blocks
methods.description: Parse SQL and prepare statement blocks for execution, considering database engine specifics.

methods.name: _finalize_successful_query
methods.description: Update query metadata and payload after successful execution, including result serialization.

methods.name: _store_results_in_backend
methods.description: Serialize and store query results in the results backend, handling size limits and errors.

methods.name: _serialize_result_set
methods.description: Serialize a result set into bytes or records, optionally using msgpack for efficiency.

methods.name: _make_check_stopped_fn
methods.description: Create a function to check if the query has been stopped.

methods.name: _make_execute_fn
methods.description: Create an execution function that wraps execution with timing metrics.

methods.name: _make_log_query_fn
methods.description: Create a function to log executed SQL queries.

methods.name: _execute_sql_statements
methods.description: Main function to execute SQL statements, handle timeouts, and process results.

methods.name: execute_sql_task
methods.description: Celery task to execute SQL asynchronously, handling context, errors, and result processing.
